name_reason: Compliant data_fd2_battle_* name for a battle-core runtime table. Descriptor accurately reflects purpose (per-glyph sprite id for the floating damage-number / MISS overlay) and data shape (a queue). The 200 dimension is carried by the array type, not the name; there is no Ghidra address residue in the name (no _53c6c-style suffix). All accessors (fd2_show_damage_number, fd2_show_miss_indicator, fd2_animate_spell_projectile_paths) confirm the semantics.
purpose: Runtime scratch queue holding the per-glyph sprite id for the floating damage-number / MISS overlay enqueued above a target's head during a battle spell/attack.
logic_summary: First of three contiguous 200-byte parallel queues that share the running index data_fd2_battle_spell_aoe_count_and_fx_queue_idx: sprite_id @ 0x53C6C, x_offset @ 0x53D34 (=0x53C6C+200), target_char_idx @ 0x53DFC (=0x53D34+200); next symbol (the index counter) sits at 0x53EC4, so the 0xC8 gap fixes the 200-byte extent. Producers append 4 entries per call and advance the index by 4: fd2_show_damage_number (@0x1E1C7) stores marker_char + digit_value - '0' for a significant decimal place, else 0 (blank place); fd2_show_miss_indicator (@0x1E258) copies a 4-byte MISS sprite run via 8-bit stores. Consumer fd2_animate_spell_projectile_paths (@0x1E012) walks slots 0..count-1, skips 0 (empty/finished), and uses the value (MOVZX, zero-extended) as a *4 index into the UI sprite sheet to fetch the glyph sprite for blitting during the 22-frame rise animation.
element_semantics: Per-slot sprite-sheet glyph id (0 = empty/blank/finished slot, skipped by the consumer; non-zero = sprite-sheet entry index used as a *4 table lookup). Unsigned 1-byte element, stride 1, proven by the 8-bit MOV stores in the producers and the MOVZX zero-extending load in the consumer.
